==English==
{{wp|MOST<dab!>}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|mōst|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈməʊst/}}
* {{enPR|mōst|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈmoʊst/}}
* {{IPA|en|[ˈmoːst]|a=CA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-most.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|əʊst|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=superlative|tree=1|:inh|enm:most<ety:inh<ang:mǣst<id:degree>>>}}
From {{inh|en|enm|most}}, {{m|enm|moste}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mǣst}}, {{m|ang|māst}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*maistaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*maist}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|mast}}, {{m|sco|maist||most}}, {{cog|stq|maast||most}}, {{cog|fy|meast||most}}, {{cog|nl|meest||most}}, {{cog|de|meist||most}}, {{cog|da|-}} and {{cog|sv|mest||most}}, {{cog|is|mestur||most}}.

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|moste||obsolete}}

====Determiner====
{{en-head|det}}

# {{superlative of|en|much}}.
#: {{ux|en|The teams competed to see who could collect (the) '''most''' money.}}
#: {{ux|en|I spent '''most''' time in Rome because '''most''' of Venice is flooded.}}
# {{superlative of|en|many}}: the comparatively largest number of ({{ng|construed with the definite article}})
#: {{ux|en|The team with the '''most''' points wins.}}
# {{superlative of|en|many}}: the majority of; more than [[half]] of; more than 50% of ({{ng|construed without the definite article}})
#: {{ux|en|'''Most''' bakers and dairy farmers have to get up early.}}
#: {{ux|en|Winning was not important for '''most''' participants.}}
#: {{ux|en|There were 100 votes cast, and 51 were in favor. That means '''most''' of the votes were in favor.}}

=====Synonyms=====
* {{sense|superlative of ''much''}} more than [[half]] of {{q|in meaning, not grammar}}, [[all]]
* {{sense|superlative of ''many''}} the [[majority]] of {{q|in meaning, not grammar}}

====Adverb====
{{en-adv|-}}

# {{ng|Forms the [[superlative]] of many adjectives.}}
#: {{ant|en|least}}
#: {{ux|en|This is the '''most''' important example.}}
#: {{ux|en|Correctness is '''most''' important.}}
#: {{ux|en|Much the '''most''' common verb in complex-intransitive clauses is ''be''.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|XII|77|{{smc|With}} some of it on the south and more of it on the north of the great main thoroughfare that connects Aldgate and the East India Docks, St. Bede's at this period of its history was perhaps the poorest and '''most''' miserable parish in the East End of London.}}
#* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=1|passage=“{{...}} the awfully hearty sort of Christmas cards that people do send to other people that they don't know at all well. You know. The kind that have mottoes{{...}}. And then, when you see [the senders], you probably find that they are the '''most''' melancholy old folk with malignant diseases. {{...}}”}}
## {{lb|en|proscribed}} {{ng|With a superlative adjective ending in {{m|en|-est}}.}}
##: {{ux|en|the '''most''' tallest building in the world}}
# To a great extent or degree; [[highly]]; [[very]].
#: {{ux|en|This is a '''most''' unusual specimen.}}
#* {{RQ:Melville Moby-Dick|chapter=The Ship|page=77|passage=A noble craft, but somehow a '''most''' melancholy!}}
#* {{RQ:Wells Time Machine|pages=114–115|pageref=114|passage=Now, I still think that for this box of matches to have escaped the wear of time for immemorial years was a most strange, as for me it was a '''most''' fortunate, thing.}}
# {{superlative of|en|much}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847|title=Boundary Problems
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21582498-america-has-changed-way-it-measures-gdp-boundary-problems
|passage=Economics is a messy discipline: too fluid to be a science, too rigorous to be an art. Perhaps it is fitting that economists’ '''most'''-used metric, gross domestic product (GDP), is a tangle too.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180221220246/https://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21582498-america-has-changed-way-it-measures-gdp-boundary-problems|archivedate=21 February 2018}}

And guess who's up for vice-president? Me! Isn't that the '''most''' to say the least?}}
# {{superlative of|en|many}}

====Pronoun====
{{en-pron}}

# The greater part of a group, especially a group of people.
#: {{ux|en|'''Most''' want the best for their children.}}
#: {{ux|en|The peach was juicier and more flavourful than '''most'''.}}

=====Synonyms=====
* {{sense|greater part}} the {{l|en|majority}}

====Noun====
{{tea room|en|m=April|y=2025}}
{{en-noun|-|s}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The greatest amount.
#: {{ux|en|The '''most''' I can offer for the house is $150,000.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|uncountable}} The greater part.
#: {{ux|en|'''Most''' of the penguins were friendly and curious.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Most''' of the rice was spoiled.}}
#* {{RQ:Besant Ivory Gate|The Select Circle|46|{{smc|At}} half-past nine on this Saturday evening the parlor of the Salutation Inn, High Holborn, contained '''most''' of its customary visitors.{{...}}In former days every tavern of repute kept such a room for the select circle—a club, or society, of ''habitués'', who met every evening for a pipe and a cheerful glass.}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|Eye Witness|249|The story struck the depressingly familiar note with which true stories ring in the tried ears of experienced policemen.{{...}}The second note, the high alarum, not so familiar and always important since it indicates the paramount sin in Man's private calendar, took '''most''' of them by surprise although they had been well prepared.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-08-16|author=[http://www.theguardian.com/profile/johnvidal John Vidal]
|volume=189|issue=10|page=8|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2013/aug/10/china-india-water-grab-dams-himalayas-danger Dams endanger ecology of Himalayas]
|passage='''Most''' of the Himalayan rivers have been relatively untouched by dams near their sources. Now the two great Asian powers, India and China, are rushing to harness them as they cut through some of the world's deepest valleys.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A [[record-setting]] amount.

=====Usage notes=====
* In the sense of {{m|en|record}}, used when the positive denotation of {{m|en|best}} does not apply.

===Etymology 2===
{{ety|en|id=almost|tree=1|text=*|:clip|almost}}

====Adverb====
{{en-adv|-}}

# {{lb|en|informal|chiefly|US}} {{clip of|en|almost}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1997|last1=Zehme|first1=Bill|authorlink1=Bill Zehme|title=The Way You Wear Your Hat: {{w|Frank Sinatra}} and the Lost Art of Livin’|isbn=978-0-06-018289-2|page=142|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/wayyouwearyourha00zehm_0/page/142/mode/1up|location2=w:Thorndike, Maine|publisher2={{w|Gale (publisher)|Thorndike Press}}|year2=1998|isbn2=978-0-7862-1437-2|page2=181|pageurl2=https://archive.org/details/wayyouwearyourha0000zehm/page/181/mode/1up|passage=Random illustration: A well-daiquiried redhead eyed him from across the room at Jilly’s one night in 1963 {{mdash}} although it could have been '''most''' any night ever {{mdash}}{{nb...|and she whimpered, “I know he’s spoiled by women, but if he crooked his little finger, I’d go with him in five seconds.”}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2000|title=Jewish Baltimore: A Family Album|page=159|isbn=0801864275
|passage="We walked there '''most''' every day after school."}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=14 April 2005|author=Stacy Smith Segovia|title=Creepy things, creatures can lurk under your home|journal=w:The Leaf-Chronicle|volume=195|issue=104|location=Clarksville, Tenn.|publisher=The Leaf-Chronicle Co.|page=D3|pageurl=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/294060942/|column=5|issn=0745-7367|oclc=9421144|passage=You’d expect to find them {{quote-gloss|black widows}} under rotting logs, but they can be '''most''' anywhere. “I’ve had them living in my barbecue grill,” {{quote-gloss|David}} Hinson says.}}

=====Usage notes=====
This use of the word must precede a noun phrase and is restricted to positive polarity. One would not say {{bad||''most nobody understands this''}} or {{bad||''I most fell down climbing up the stairs''}}.
